clue.text: Dance in prison

definitions.meaning: a West Indian dance in which one bends back under a lowered bar
old slang for a jail or place of confinement

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a bar-dancing routine and, in old slang, a jail cell where one is held.

clue.text: Counsel to reform and stop recording

indicators.note: reform means re-form, so the letters of counsel and to are reshaped

explanation.surface: Advice to change one's ways and stop keeping records.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose track of a tally is to stop keeping the score.

clue.text: 7-1 — walk-over

indicators.note: over means the pieces are turned round, read backwards

parts.note: the figure 1 resembles the letter I
roam means walk, wander

explanation.surface: A sporting score followed by an easy win.
explanation.walkthrough: '7' is the answer to 7 down (ABORIGINE): a Maori is a native New Zealander. 'over' turns I ROAM back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand.

clue.text: Getting warm place for gymnastic exercises

definitions.meaning: on the right track, close to the answer
the balance bar where gymnasts perform

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means on course, nearly right, and also literally atop the balance bar a gymnast uses.

clue.text: Settle sectarian differences

indicators.note: differences suggest the letters of the word sectarian are set at odds and rearranged

explanation.surface: A call to resolve quarrels between religious factions.
explanation.definitionFit: To settle a question is to find out for certain, establish the facts.

clue.text: Bill Lock, one in play

parts.note: AC is short for account, a bill
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A character named Bill Lock appears in a drama.
explanation.definitionFit: An actress is a woman performing in a stage drama.

clue.text: Put top on glue — it's upset

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the first piece comes first

parts.note: to cap is to put a top on
size is a gluey sizing liquid

explanation.surface: Replace the lid on the glue pot, it has been knocked over.
explanation.definitionFit: To capsize is to overturn, as a boat is upset.

clue.text: Show travelled round.

parts.note: rode means travelled on horseback
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A touring show.
explanation.definitionFit: A rodeo is a public exhibition of cowboy skills.

clue.text: Oldest inhabitant from a source in Lincoln

indicators.note: in means the word for source goes inside the name for Lincoln

parts.note: Abraham Lincoln, known as Abe
an origin is a source

explanation.surface: Tracing the oldest resident's roots to Lincoln.
explanation.definitionFit: An aborigine is one of the earliest known people of a land.

clue.text: … loses his shirt perhaps, being gullible

indicators.note: loses means a letter is dropped from the word carried over from the previous clue

parts.note: the ellipsis carries on from 7 down, whose oldest inhabitant is a native
a T-shirt, so T is his shirt

explanation.surface: An innocent local is fleeced and left without a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to 7 down: its 'Oldest inhabitant' gives NATIVE, which 'loses' its T (as in T-shirt) to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Naive means credulous, innocently trusting.

clue.text: Baseball player taking time-out

definitions.meaning: a fielder stationed between second and third base
a brief halt or pause, read as two words

explanation.surface: A ballplayer resting during a game.
explanation.definitionFit: The fielding position's name, split in two, also describes a brief pause in play.

clue.text: Lawrence with the Japanese sash he washes

parts.note: D. H. Lawrence, the English novelist, gives his initials
an obi is the broad sash worn with a kimono

explanation.surface: A novelist wearing a kimono sash does the laundry.
explanation.walkthrough: A dhobi is a washerman in India, a word familiar from British India.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a dhobi is a man whose trade is laundering clothes.

clue.text: Many wrong retreating but victorious general

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for 100, a large number

indicators.note: retreating means the word for wrong is read backwards

parts.note: wrong means evil, wickedness

explanation.surface: A general who won despite many errors and a retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Clive, 'Clive of India', won at Plassey in 1757; 'retreating' turns EVIL to LIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Clive of India was the British commander famed for his victories in Bengal.

clue.text: To sum up, 10 empties to be collected

indicators.note: collected in the sense of composed or put together, so the letters are reassembled

parts.note: the figures 1 and 0 are read as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: In short, ten empty bottles await pickup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'be collected' makes the letters of IO plus EMPTIES rearrange; the trick is reading 10 as I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: To epitomise something is to sum it up in a brief typical example.

clue.text: Economise in vain

parts.note: to economise is to use less
the second half of the phrase use less

explanation.surface: Trying to save money proves pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Effort spent in vain is futile, achieving nothing.

clue.text: Makes proper use of taxes the sovereign introduced

indicators.note: introduced means the sovereign's letters are put inside the taxes

parts.note: excises are duties on goods
ER is the Queen, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The monarch levied taxes and spends them wisely.
explanation.definitionFit: To exercise a right is to put it to use.

clue.text: Head not shown in attractive picture

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for attractive is left off

parts.note: fetching means attractive, charming

explanation.surface: A pretty portrait with the face cropped out.
explanation.definitionFit: An etching is a print made from an acid-bitten plate, a kind of picture.

clue.text: Replies conversely "Go forwards"

parts.note: conversely, the opposite of go is come
conversely, the opposite of forwards in rugby is backs

explanation.surface: Answers put the other way round: Go forwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conversely' tells you to replace each word with its opposite; in rugby the forwards are matched by the backs.
explanation.definitionFit: Comebacks are quick retorts or replies.

clue.text: Persuaded great PM to climb up and drop off

parts.note: got someone to do something, persuaded
OS is outsize

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing up means the prime minister's name is read upwards

parts.note: Robert Peel, British prime minister

explanation.surface: Someone talked a great prime minister into climbing and then nodded off.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is to fall asleep.

clue.text: Mother's unusual means of keeping warm

indicators.note: unusual marks the letters of mother's as arranged in an odd new way

parts.note: the letters of mother's including the s

explanation.surface: Mum has her own odd way of staying warm.
explanation.definitionFit: A vacuum flask keeps drinks hot; the brand name became generic.

clue.text: Around Dover, prize appears off-shore

parts.note: Dover is in the south-east of England, SE
an award is a prize

explanation.surface: A prize turns up near the coast at Dover.
explanation.definitionFit: Seaward means towards the open sea, away from land.

clue.text: Joint medical speciality that's brilliant

parts.note: a joint of meat, such as lamb
ENT is ear, nose and throat medicine

explanation.surface: A hospital department that specialises in joints is outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambent means softly glowing or flickering, hence brilliant or radiant.

clue.text: The girl has changed, having lost weight

indicators.note: changed means the letters of the girl are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: She has become a different person since slimming.
explanation.definitionFit: Lighter means weighing less.

clue.text: Supports archbishop, in a manner of speaking

parts.note: backs means supports, as in backing a candidate
Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury 1928 to 1942

explanation.surface: A churchman's backers engage in a way of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: Back slang is British slang that says words backwards (yob from boy).
explanation.definitionFit: Back slang is a slang code formed by saying words backwards, a way of talking.

clue.text: Muddle up fare some days

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: to fare is to go on, get along
February is a group of days, abbreviated Feb

explanation.surface: Bus fares go up on some days, confusing passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: To befog is to confuse, obscure.

clue.text: Authority keeps mum

parts.note: to keep mum is to say nothing, says
nothing, nought, is O

explanation.surface: The person in charge stays silent.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's say-so is their authorisation.

clue.text: In Slough, starts to utter specie that's counterfeit

parts.note: a slough is a bog or swamp

indicators.note: the initial letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: In the town of Slough, someone begins to pass false coin.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough is also an English town, which is the surface's misdirection; to utter is to pass off false money.
explanation.definitionFit: Bogus means fake, sham, not genuine.

clue.text: Simpleton employed by a tailor

explanation.definitionFit: The bird's name is used for a fool and also for a tailor's heavy pressing iron.

clue.text: Turn back if the experiment is dubious

indicators.note: turn back means the little word if is read backwards

parts.note: a shy is a try or attempt, as in having a shy at something

explanation.surface: Advice to abandon a doubtful test.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fishy is suspicious, of questionable honesty.

clue.text: Flower pictures I suppress

parts.note: art means pictures, paintings
to choke back is to suppress

explanation.surface: Someone stifles the urge to paint flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe artichoke is the edible bud of a thistle-like flower head.

clue.text: Cut obsolescent fuel store

parts.note: a gash is a deep cut
obsolescent means getting older, out of date

explanation.surface: Funding is cut for an ageing fuel tank.
explanation.walkthrough: A gasholder is a large tank storing town gas, a familiar sight in British towns.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasometer is a large tank holding coal gas for supply.

clue.text: Gambling row

definitions.meaning: a sweepstake, a lottery where the pot goes to the winner
to row with a long oar

explanation.definitionFit: The word is short for sweepstake, a kind of lottery, and is also a long oar used to propel a boat.
